title: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection - Crystal Originated Particles (COP) Detection on Zeta-388
subtitle: Post-Lithography Quality Validation for 7nm Node Manufacturing
author: Maria Gonzalez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-388 system to detect and classify Crystal Originated Particles (COP) defects during post-lithography inspection at the 7nm technology node. The test is conducted at Singapore Fab 7 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Crystal Originated Particles (COP) defects that are critical to yield at the 7nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-388 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-388
- Inspection Type: Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: Crystal Originated Particles (COP)
- Process Step: Post-Lithography
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 7nm
- Fab Location: Singapore Fab 7

This test case applies to all Zeta-388 systems deployed at Singapore Fab 7 for post-lithography monitoring in the 7nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-388
Software Version: v10.2.608
Recipe: UNPATTERNED_WAFER_INSPECTION_7nm_POST_LITHOGRAPHY
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Medium (103 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-388 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Unpatterned Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Crystal Originated Particles (COP) defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 7nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 115 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 99% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.8% for Unpatterned Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.96 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-04-07
Wafers Tested: 5
Total Defects Found: 944
Defect Density: 300.48 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.7%
Capture Rate: 96.4%
Test Duration: 334 minutes
System Uptime: 98.1%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-388 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Crystal Originated Particles (COP) at the 7nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
